chapter: Eddie Heywood, the organ and later work
title: Bill Doggett and "Honky Tonk"
summary: Doggett made hits and shrewdly invested; "Honky Tonk" sold a million.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: Well, Wild Bill Davis, and who came next? Bill Doggett?
Yeah, Bill Doggett. Often they were confused, you know. But Doggett, he went far ...(?)...
Well, I've got a record that he made in Paris with a guitar player and I think a tenor player about a year ago, and it's a beautiful record! It's not just a funky thing.
Bill Doggett seemed to fade out of the picture. He had some great years, didn't he.
Yes, he did. Because he made them all at one time, and then he released them periodically as singles.

"Honky Tonk" sold a million. He had more hits than Wild Bill Davis. For him it was a smart business move. But he told me, he said, "Ram, you must get in on this now." He had been playing for Ella, you see, and he was making
good money. He was on several hits with Ella. Then he took that money and he parlayed it, and he stayed ...(?). for years.
Well, maybe he's got a lot of money salted away.
He's got a great big reservation out there in Central Islip or something.
